title: CRLR/198/2014 of Ms. Sahajahan Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
CRLR No. 198 of 2014
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Dy. A.G. for the
State.
Heard.
Present criminal revision has been
preferred by the revisionist against the order
dated 21.07.2014 in Criminal Case No. 1071
of 2009 ìState Vs. Anees Ahamad & Ors.
under Section 498-A, 323, 504 & 506 I.P.C.
and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act passed by
learned Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur District
Udham Singh Nagar, whereby the revisionist
has been summoned under Section 319
Cr.P.C.
Brief facts of the case are that the
complainant/second respondent has lodged
F.I.R. against the husband and some other
relative of his husband. After completion of
investigation a chargesheet has been filed
against the husband-revisionist. The trial has
been commenced. During the trial, the second
respondent has filed an application under
Section 319 Cr.P.C. before learned Judicial
Magistrate, Kashipur, District Udham Singh
Nagar alleging therein that her sister-in-law
has also committed offence. The Judicial
Magistrate by impugned order dated
21.07.2014 has summoned the
revisionist/sister-in-law of the second
respondent.
During the pendency of present criminal
revision, the second respondent entered into a
compromise with the husband as well as
other family members of the husband.
The mediation was held in presence of
the parties by Ms. Anjali Bhargava,
Advocate/Mediator and Mr. R.C. Khulbe,
Registrar (Incharge Mediation). The husband
agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 4.00 lakh to
the wife-second respondent and Rs. 1.00 lakh
to her daughter on her attaining the age of

majority. However, as the file of mediation
could not be traced despite orders of this
Court, parties were directed to appear in
person before the Court.
Today, the second respondent and
revisionist are present in person duly
identified by their counsel.
Second respondent-Smt. Shamim Jahan
makes a statement at bar the matter has
already been amicable settled between her
and her husband that she has also received
an amount of Rs. 4 lacs from the husband
and that remaining amount of Rs. 1 lacs shall
be paid by the husband when her daughter
will attain the age of majority. The second
respondent does not wish to continue the
Criminal Case No. 1071 of 2019.
Having considered the submissions of
husband and second respondent, this Court
is of the firm opinion that the compromise has
taken placed between the husband and wife-second respondent as such the continuation
of criminal proceedings against the revisionist
pursuant to the impugned F.I.R. would be a
futile exercise and no useful purpose would
be served to keep the same pending against
the revisionist as well as against husband and
other family members. The impugned order
dated 21.07.2014 is hereby quashed. The
proceedings of Criminal Case No. 1071 of
2019, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504 & 506
of I.P.C. pending in the Court of Judicial
Magistrate, Kashipur, District Udham Singh
Nagar is hereby quashed.
The criminal revision stands disposed of
accordingly.
(Lok Pal Singh, J.)
 26.03.2019
Mamta
